question: What is the primary goal of hospital equipment management in a clinical ward?

options.A: Preventing nurses from having to buy personal tools
options.C: Reducing the overall budget of the hospital pharmacy
options.D: Ensuring items are ready and safe for patient care

explanation: Equipment management focuses entirely on keeping clinical tools functional, safe, and readily available to support patient treatment. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is taking good care of equipment especially important in Nigerian healthcare settings where resources can be scarce?

options.A: It extends the lifespan of scarce clinical assets
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for biomedical engineers
options.C: It replaces the need for standard nursing documentation
options.D: It allows wards to hoard supplies away from other units

explanation: You've got this! When replacements are hard to come by, keeping our current tools well-maintained ensures we can always care for our patients without interruption. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is classified as a consumable clinical item?
explanation: Consumables are single-use items that get discarded immediately after a single clinical procedure. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h2)

question: A patient monitor is best described by which category of hospital equipment?
explanation: Capital equipment refers to durable, high-cost items that are kept for long-term use across multiple patients. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why must we always wash instruments to remove dirt before trying to sterilize them?

options.A: Cleaning makes the metal surface shiny and attractive to look at
options.B: Dried blood and protein block sterilizing agents from reaching microbes
options.C: Sterilization chemicals will otherwise stain the hospital linens
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of operating the autoclave machine

explanation: Think of dried blood like a protective shield for germs! If we don't wash it off first, the heat or steam can't get underneath to kill them. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization destroys bacterial spores, whereas disinfection does not
options.B: Sterilization uses plain tap water while disinfection uses pure alcohol
options.C: Disinfection takes place only in the hospital laundry department
options.D: Disinfection is reserved exclusively for surgical theatre floors

explanation: Sterilization achieves total destruction of all microbial life including hardy spores, whereas disinfection reduces pathogens to a safe level but may leave spores behind. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h3)

question: What happens if you wipe down a blood pressure cuff with disinfectant and dry it off immediately?

options.A: The velcro straps will lose their sticky properties forever
options.B: The mercury inside the gauge will solidify permanently
options.C: The disinfectant does not get enough contact time to kill the microbes
options.D: The fabric of the cuff will instantly dissolve in the solution

explanation: Disinfectants need a little time to sit wet on a surface to do their germ-killing magic. Wiping them dry instantly stops them from working! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h4)

question: A nurse finishes checking a patient's blood pressure with a shared manual sphygmomanometer. What action should be taken next?

options.A: Decontaminate the cuff with an approved disinfectant before the next patient
options.B: Return the cuff straight to the duty station drawer without cleaning
options.C: Wash the entire fabric cuff inside the washing machine with laundry soap
options.D: Spray the patient's arm with antiseptic lotion instead of cleaning the cuff

explanation: Shared non-invasive equipment like blood pressure cuffs must be wiped down between patients to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is a recommended practice when storing idle electronic clinical equipment?

options.A: Leaving power cords dangling loosely across the walkway
options.B: Using dust covers to prevent particulate accumulation in vents
options.C: Placing machines directly on damp floors to keep them cool
options.D: Exposing the device to direct sunlight to eliminate moisture

explanation: Dust covers protect sensitive machinery from dust and debris entering internal cooling vents and delicate electronic pathways. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why must infusion pumps and suction machines be secured properly during transport within a hospital?

options.A: To prevent physical damage and loss of calibration from drops
options.B: To ensure the battery never loses its charge while moving
options.C: To allow patients to operate the buttons while being wheeled
options.D: To make the machine look more professional to visitors

explanation: Rough handling or accidental drops can knock delicate internal components out of alignment and break fragile casings. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the first step a nurse should take after discovering a clinical device is faulty?

options.A: Leave it plugged in at the bedside for the next shift to handle
options.B: Throw the expensive machine directly into the general waste bin
options.C: Attempt to repair the internal microchips using a screwdriver
options.D: Remove it from service and attach a clear warning tag

explanation: Isolating the broken device and labeling it prevents accidental use on patients while waiting for repairs. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is an appropriate initial troubleshooting step when an electric monitor fails to turn on?

options.A: Checking if the power cord is firmly plugged into the socket
options.B: Disassembling the internal motherboard to check the wiring
options.C: Writing off the machine as permanently damaged immediately
options.D: Submerging the entire device in sterile water to clean it

explanation: Simple power supply checks should always be performed first before suspecting complex internal mechanical failure. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous and unprofessional for a nurse to use complex life-support equipment without proper training?

options.A: It breaks the personal promise made during the graduation ceremony
options.B: It places the patient at high risk of preventable injury or death
options.C: It wastes electricity in the hospital ward unnecessarily
options.D: It forces the biomedical engineers to work extra hours

explanation: Patient safety always comes first! Operating specialized devices without proper training puts vulnerable lives in serious, preventable danger. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h7)

question: A student nurse notices a pulse oximeter has a broken cable giving wild readings, but uses it anyway because nothing else is around. What rule has been broken?

options.A: Duty of care and patient safety

explanation: Using broken equipment puts our patients at risk. As midwives, our greatest commitment is to keep our mothers and babies safe! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h7)
